fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Outdoor Storage Area; Detached Structure; Open Terrain; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials could significantly improve responder ingress and egress, particularly given the limited alternatives for rear access. Posting visible address signage near the street frontage and at the driveway entry would support faster navigation to the correct access point. Maintaining adequate clearance along the driveway corridor may assist larger emergency vehicles in maneuvering to the main building and detached structure. Keeping the outdoor storage area organized and set back from primary travel paths could facilitate unobstructed movement and staging during an emergency response.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Dense Shrub Cover; Heavy Brush; Continuous Shrub Cover; Scattered Trees; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Fuel Continuity; Limited Defensible Space; Brushland Interface; Vegetated Access Route; Single Access Route; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the density and continuity of shrub cover and heavy brush in the immediate area surrounding the structure would meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce the opportunity for fire to spread directly to the building. Creating and maintaining separation between brush and the structure's exterior, including walls, vents, decks, and other attachments, may reduce direct fuel contact and improve conditions for suppression operations. Thinning and spacing vegetation between shrub masses and scattered trees could reduce vertical and horizontal fuel continuity throughout the property. Given that access to the property relies on a single vegetated route, maintaining cleared and navigable conditions along that driveway or access road is a priority, as it supports both firefighter ingress and occupant egress during an emergency. Keeping that corridor free of encroaching brush and low-hanging vegetation would support reliable two-way access and improve visibility along the route, contributing to long-term wildfire resilience and property preparedness.
